svg.text: Top: the front, where the parts go. Bottom: the back, where you solder. It is flipped left-to-right, like turning the board over.
lever sticks out of the bottom edge
Both screens sit along the top edge,
with their header pins in row 1.
The SuperMini lies sideways in the
bottom right. Its USB-C hangs over
the right edge so you can plug it in.
The button goes in the gap between
The switch goes on the bottom edge.
Nothing else goes on the front.
The wires, the TP4056 charger and
the battery all go on the back.
Drawn for a 30 × 37 mm TFT board,
a 27 × 27 mm OLED board and a
vary a little. Push everything into
the holes before soldering, then move
a part by one hole if it doesn't fit.
LiPo battery: goes on LAST, on top of kapton tape
Wires are drawn straight here. Real ones can
bend however you like: keep them flat.
A wire that only passes a pin isn't joined
to it. Joins are only at the wire ends.
Board GND takes wires 2 and 3. Button leg A
Button: use the diagonal legs A and D.
Check every pin name against the printing
on your own boards before soldering.
Seen from the back, the TFT is on the RIGHT and the SuperMini on the LEFT.
Column numbers run 24 → 1. Full pin table: WIRING.md
